Rolling Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders for metal and plastic operate rolling mills and calendering equipment; set tooling and adjust roll gaps; monitor thickness, tension, and temperature curves; take samples and measure thickness; and adjust equipment for specification changes to ensure consistent dimensions and properties in strip and sheet materials.

paragraphs: At shift handover, first review process cards and roll condition. After installing and aligning rolls, start the line and monitor the thickness curve as the steel strip passes through. Fine-tune the roll gap and tension when measurements exceed tolerance. Take intermediate samples for thickness measurement, then stop the line to adjust rolls and change dies when specifications change. Rush in to clear jams or strip breaks, and before leaving, inspect equipment, clean rolls, complete records, and document the first-piece result.

In short: compress thick material into qualified thin strip according to specified parameters. CNC machines cut blanks into parts, while rolling machines compress thick material into strip or sheet, so the operating principles differ. Rolling places greater emphasis on roll gaps, tension, temperature, and continuous production lines, while CNC work emphasizes tool setting, tool compensation, and individual-part precision. Both are highly skilled operating roles.
